chapter_theme: The third part of the woman's lament is mostly praise of him to her friend: the one body unbroken in every direction, the supreme light set in the sea of devotion, the awareness of awareness, without root or top, undiminished by all the beings in all the worlds, the Full One without speech, mind or form, easy to see and not seen, the light in the ruby, inside and outside atom and Meru, the clarity of the sugarcane of knowledge. Then the story resumes: he held her as the hold of those who hold nothing, dwelt in her in open space while everyone watched in daylight, gave her a life that is not living and a true life that is bare void; the virgin palm bore fruit, every place smells of civet, and he swallowed her as hot iron drinks water and fire eats camphor.
structure_note: 557 to 568 are the -அடி and -காண் descriptions of him; 569 to 576 return to what he did to her and what she saw; 577 to 581 close in wonder with four images of absorption (the fruiting palm, the civet scent, iron and water, fire and camphor). The part ends at 581 and the work continues into a fourth part. All units are from the single source and printed without word spacing.

557.reading: His state is one the ten directions cannot contain; he is the one body, unbroken everywhere, in every direction.
557.nuance: ஏகம், the one, and இடைவிடாது, without gap, state pervasion as a single continuous body rather than as presence in many places. பருவம் here is state or condition rather than season.

558.reading: He wells up sweetly for those who have the mind for it; he is the supreme light set within the sea of devotion.
558.nuance: தித்திக்க ஊறும், welling sweetly like juice, is the first of the chapter's taste images (the sugarcane of 566 follows). The verse makes devotion the sea the light is set in, after 553 blamed the lack of devotion for the fall.

559.reading: He is the awareness of the awareness of those who stand as inner awareness; by not even a sesame's measure does he rise above what is, nor fall short of it.
559.nuance: உணர்வுக்கு உணர்வு, awareness of awareness, is repeated at 556 as knowledge of knowledge. எள்ளளவும் உள்ளதிலே ஏறிக் குறையான் is read as neither more nor less than what is: he is exactly the real, without excess or lack.

560.reading: He has no root and no top, no arising and no subsiding; unknown to anyone he stood as the undivided.
560.nuance: தூரும் தலையும் இலான், without root or head, is the Tamil way of saying beginningless and endless; தோற்றம் ஒடுக்கம் denies him the arising and dissolution that everything made undergoes. அகண்டம் is the unbroken whole.

561.reading: However many beings there are in however many worlds, though all of them exist, he is not lessened by an atom.
561.nuance: The verse answers an implied objection: if he is everything, the many lives would divide him. அணுவும் குறையான் denies it, and the next verses keep the atom as the measure (566).

562.reading: He is the vast thing without speech, mind or form, without going or coming, the incomparable Full One.
562.nuance: பூரணன், the Full One, is the Siddhars' name for God as fullness, and here it is defined by what he lacks: speech, mind, form and motion. வான்பொருள் may be 'the great thing' or 'the thing that is sky'.

563.reading: He is easy to see, and even when seen is not seen here; for those who set a noble mind on him, he is the light within the ruby.
563.nuance: காட்சிக்கு எளியான் is the Kural's phrase for an accessible king, turned on the Lord. கண்டாலும் இங்கு காணான் is the paradox that seeing him is not seeing him as he is. மாணிக்கத்துள் ஒளி returns from 550.

564.reading: Even if one praises him and worships him, he is the one whom enduring lives find hard to see; he is the light beyond words.
564.nuance: The syntax is loose: வாழ்த்தியவனை வழிபட்டால் (if one worships him who is praised) is followed by மன்னுயிர்கள் தோற்றவரியான், hard for lives to see, so that praise and worship do not by themselves bring sight. Another reading has தோற்ற as 'appear', he who rarely appears to lives.

565.reading: If there are any who inquire into the one who has cut off doubt, he will come into the world and set down his flower feet.
565.nuance: ஐயம் is doubt, and also alms: ஐயம் அறுத்தவன் can be the one who ends doubt or the beggar-saint who has ended begging, and Pattinathar lived by alms. The verse makes inquiry (ஆராய்தல்) the condition of his coming.

566.reading: He stood inside and outside both the atom and Meru; he is the clear juice of the sugarcane of knowledge, ripe in every joint.
566.nuance: அணுவுக்கும் மேருவுக்கும் அகம்புறம், within and without the least and the greatest, is pervasion stated in extremes. கணு முற்றும், every joint ripe, makes knowledge a sugarcane with no unripe node, and தெளிவு its clear juice.

567.reading: At any time, at this time, 'thus' and 'so': however he is told, he does not hear; he does not take it in through the ear.
567.nuance: சோத்திரம் is the ear (Sanskrit shrotra). The verse may mean that no description reaches him, since he is beyond hearing as beyond speech (562); or, as complaint, that he cannot be moved by pleading. The first fits the -காண் series.

568.reading: He is mother to the mother and father to the father; for those who string him into a frame he is the sea of qualities that takes the strung state.
568.nuance: கோத்தார்க்குக் கோத்த நிலை கொண்ட, taking for those who string the state they string, says that he fits whatever doctrine frames him; 547 had the speaker's own strung doctrine collapse. The sea of qualities is a Lord with attributes for those who need them.

569.reading: Is it new now? How many days it has been! Moment by moment he gave me grace and understanding.
569.nuance: இப்போ புதிதோடி is read as a question to the friend, 'is this new now?', with the answer that it has been so for a long time (எத்தனை நாள் உள்ளது). அப்போதைக்கு அப்போது, moment to moment, makes grace continuous rather than a single event.

570.reading: He held me as the hold of those who hold to nothing; he cut off my fault; he stayed joined with me.
570.nuance: பற்று அற்றார் பற்றாக, as the attachment of the unattached: he is the one thing those who have let go still hold, and here it is he who holds her. கூடியிருந்தான், he stayed united, carries the bridal sense.

571.reading: He dwelt in me in the open space; everyone stood watching, in broad daylight.
571.nuance: வெட்டவெளி, the open expanse of 529, is where the union happens; பட்டப்பகலில் பார்த்திருந்தார் எல்லோரும் is the scandal of 530 again, everyone watching, and also the point of 575, that all saw and none knew.

572.reading: A life that is truly life came to me, without my living it; without sinking I sank, and nothing was lacking.
572.nuance: Two paradoxes, வாழாமல் வாழ்வு and தாழாமல் தாழ்ந்தேன்: the true life is not lived as a life, and the lowering is not a fall. சற்றும் குறையாமல், with no lack, echoes the Lord who is not lessened (561).

573.reading: The false life: I saw that I had had enough of it. The true life: for me it turned into bare void.
573.nuance: வெறும் பாழாய் விட்டது, 'became mere void', can be heard as loss or as the attainment: the true life, when it comes, is the emptiness of 548 and 545. The verse does not decide, and that is its tone throughout the lament.

574.reading: I saw with my eyes full the one who destroyed my maidenhood; I do not know my own nature; what maya is this!
574.nuance: கன்னி அழித்தவன் is the taker of 531, now seen face to face. மாயம் here is wonder or trick rather than the cosmic maya; என் இயல்பு நான் அறியேன் is the knower who knew herself at 528 now not knowing what she is.

575.reading: To say it in words there is no mouth to say it; everyone has seen it and sat there, and yet they do not know it now.
575.nuance: சொல்ல வாய் இல்லை, no mouth or no way to say it. The second line turns 571 round: those who watched in daylight saw and did not understand.

576.reading: He cast a spell on my eyes and I lost my purpose; I saw the one who cast the spell lose his form.
576.nuance: கண்மாயம் is conjuring, a trick on the eyes. புண்மாயம் in line 2 is obscure (புண் is a wound); it may be a rhyme-echo or a corruption of புன்மாயம், petty illusion. உருவழியக் கண்டேன், I saw him lose his form, answers the question of 518: he came as form to destroy form, and the form went too.

577.reading: What am I to say of this wonder? Before my eyes the young virgin areca palm bore fruit.
577.nuance: கன்னி இளங்கமுகு காய்த்தது, a virgin palm fruiting, is the paradox of 528 (the taken one is a maiden) made into an image: the fruit is read by tradition as knowledge or release born in the soul without a worldly cause. The verse only calls it a wonder (அதிசயம்).

578.reading: Every place that is filled is grace itself; every place that is reached smells of civet.
578.nuance: சவாது is civet, the perfume of lovers and courtesans in the Thiruppugazh; here it is the scent of grace wherever one goes. ஆர்ந்த (filled) and சார்ந்த (joined) rhyme the Lord's fullness with the soul's approach.

579.reading: Knowing this scent everywhere to be the natural scent, I sank into that sea of grace that is beyond pleasure.
579.nuance: இயற்கை மணம், the natural scent, is not applied like a courtesan's perfume but innate. சுகாதீதம், beyond pleasure, places the sea of grace past even bliss; the sinking (மூழ்கினேன்) begins the absorption images of 580 and 581.

580.reading: He swallowed me as water is taken up by hot iron; he stayed as if he were not there, like the fragrance in a bud.
580.nuance: இரும்பு நிறை நீர், water on iron, is the Tirumanthiram's image of absorption without remainder; அரும்பு நிறை வாசனை, scent filling a bud, is presence that cannot be pointed to. அன்றே இருந்தான் is read as 'he was there as if not', or 'he was so from that very day'.

581.reading: Like fire that swallows camphor leaving nothing, he stayed joined within me, merged into me.
581.nuance: Camphor in fire leaves no ash; the image is of a union with no residue. மக்கினம் பட்டு is obscure; மக்கி means to rot or dissolve, and 'dissolved into me' is the guess taken here. The part ends on the inside (உள்ளே) after a chapter of 'everywhere'.

links.note: Tirumular says there is one God in all ten directions and no direction where he is not; Pattinathar says his state is not contained by the ten directions and he is one body unbroken in every direction. Pattinathar's verse has no refuge or deeds, only the pervasion.

Both deny that pervasion lessens him: Tirumular's Lord, being everywhere as all that moves and does not, stands without lessening; Pattinathar's is not lessened by an atom though every being in every world exists.

The light within the ruby twice in the same lament: at 550 he stays mingled in the speaker like that light, and at 563 he is that light for those who set a noble mind on him. The first is indwelling, the second the condition of seeing it.

At 547 the speaker's strung doctrine collapsed when she saw all as the Supreme; 568 adds that for those who string a frame he takes the strung state, so the collapse is hers and not a fault in those who hold a doctrine.

The Kural says to cling to the clinging of the one who has no clinging, in order to let clinging go; Pattinathar says he held her as the hold of those who hold to nothing. The Kural commands the soul to hold; Pattinathar has the Lord do the holding.
Pattinathar tells his heart elsewhere that to stay in the open space without liking or disliking is joy; here, in the woman's voice, he dwelt in her in that open space.

Tirumular takes the void as his way and rests in the void that has dropped even that imagining; Pattinathar says the true life became bare void for her. Both make the void the end and not a loss, though Pattinathar leaves the tone open.
518 asks whether he came as a form or to destroy form; 576 answers with what she saw, the one who cast the spell losing his own form.

Tirumular's virgin, and virgin undone, bore the five gods; Pattinathar's virgin palm bore fruit. In Tirumular the paradox belongs to Shakti as mother; in Pattinathar to the soul taken by the Lord, whose maidenhood was destroyed at 531 and who is a maiden again at 528.

In the Thiruppugazh civet is the scent of women who seek money with deceitful hearts; in Pattinathar every place reached smells of civet, and 579 calls it the natural scent of grace. The same perfume is applied in one and innate in the other.

The same image in the same words: Tirumular's Nandi drew him in as hot iron draws in water (இரும்பிடை நீர்); Pattinathar's Lord swallowed her like water taken up by iron (இரும்பு நிறை நீர்). Both are of absorption with nothing left over.

Tirumular's streaming body goes into the Supreme like camphor in a rising flame; Pattinathar's Lord swallows her like fire eating camphor without remainder. In Tirumular the image is of the body's ending, in Pattinathar of the union itself.

source_issues: All units 557 to 581 come from the single source pmuni0276_01 and are printed without word spacing, so word division is the marker's; the readings of 564, 567 and 581 depend on it.
576 line 2 புண்மாயம் is probably a rhyme-echo of கண்மாயம் or a corruption of புன்மாயம்; the text is kept as printed.
581 line 2 மக்கினம்பட்டு is an obscure form, perhaps for மக்கிப்பட்டு or a variant spelling.
